question.text: Part C of the PMLA Schedule deals with:

answer.text: Offences related to customs duty evasion above Rs. 1 crore
Offences related to insider trading in securities markets
Offences with cross-border implications, including those specified in Part A and offences against property under Chapter XVII of the IPC

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pp.57-58, 67), Part C of the PMLA Schedule covers offences with cross-border implications. It includes (1) offences specified in Part A with cross-border implications, (2) offences against property under Chapter XVII of the Indian Penal Code, and (3) the offence of wilful attempt to evade tax under section 51 of the Black Money Act, 2015. The Trap: Customs offences sit elsewhere in the Schedule, not Part C. Insider trading is a Part A offence (SEBI Act). Part C has no monetary threshold — it focuses specifically on the cross-border nature of the offence. Note: Use IPC Chapter XVII for the Part C property-offence limb. The Black Money Act section 51 tax-evasion offence is also part of the Part C list.
